The '''Q-series droideka''' was a model of [[Droideka/Legends|destroyer droid]] employed by the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]]. It was used mainly during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], and was produced by the [[Phlac-Arphocc Automata Industries/Legends|Phlac-Arphocc Automata Industries]]. It served on various [[Capital ship/Legends|capital ships]], such as the [[Invisible Hand/Legends|''Invisible Hand'']]. It also proved to be a lethal asset on the battlefield with its [[Personal energy shield/Legends|personal energy shield]], but became vulnerable, like other droideka models, if rolling along on the battlefront, as their shield could not be activated during this time.

They were mainly used by the [[Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation]] and the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]]. The CIS were able to receive special discounts on these [[Droid/Legends|droids]] by bribing the carnivorous [[Colicoid/Legends|Colicoids]], the creators of the droideka, with meat.

==Characteristics==
{{Quote|Droidekas are fast&hellip; very fast.|[[Urai Fen]]|<ref name="Star Wars: Empire at War: Forces of Corruption">''[[Star Wars: Empire at War: Forces of Corruption]]''</ref>}}
The Q-series droidekas were more formidable than the Trade Federation's many B1 battle droids for several reasons. They were able to transform into a wheel-like configuration, allowing rapid movement and compact storage.<ref name="Episode I: The Visual Dictionary" /> When they encountered their targets, the [[Bronzium/Legends|bronzium]]-armored droids would unfold into a tripodal weapons platform, equipped with powerful, built-in twin [[Blaster/Legends|blasters]] and often [[Personal energy shield/Legends|personal shield]] generators. These [[Deflector shield/Legends|shield]] generators could endure much punishment, and were capable of deflecting or absorbing any manner of firepower up to a light [[Artillery/Legends|artillery]] bolt,<ref name="LOE">''[[Labyrinth of Evil]]''</ref> as well as [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]] blades and physical attacks, among other weaponry. Additionally, the effectiveness of these droids was bolstered by the lack of true [[Photoreceptor/Legends|photoreceptors]]; instead, droidekas utilized non-visual composite radiation [[Sensor/Legends|sensors]], less likely to be distracted by mere light-based trickery.<ref name="Episode I: The Visual Dictionary" />
[[Droideka dispenser]]s were sometimes used as transport and dispense for these droids. They were capable of deploying droidekas right into a combat zone, and proved a nuisance to enemy troops for this reason.<ref name="Episode I: The Visual Dictionary" />

This model of droideka was an upgrade of the [[W-series droideka/Legends|W-series droideka]]. There were not very many differences in design, except for a shinier coating which was also a darker shade of red, as well as slightly increased firepower in the Q-series droideka. The new series also did not overheat as quickly as previous versions.<ref name="Revenge of the Sith: Incredible Cross-Sections" /> A number of Q-series droidekas served aboard the [[Invisible Hand/Legends|''Invisible Hand'']] during the [[Battle of Coruscant/Legends|Battle of Coruscant]]. Two fired at Jedi Master [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] and his former [[Padawan/Legends|Padawan]], [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]], on the ship, however, the two Jedi escaped by entering an elevator.<ref name="Revenge of the Sith: Incredible Cross-Sections" /><ref name="rots" />

===Design flaws===
Despite being a very formidable droid, the droideka had one major design flaw. Its shield was designed to enclose the droideka in a standing position, but if the droid was to be knocked on its side or against a wall, the shield would have no way of distinguishing the wall or floor from a blaster rifle or lightsaber. This meant that the shield generator had to continue supplying energy to the shield, resulting in an overload, as demonstrated during the rescue on the [[Invisible Hand/Legends|''Invisible Hand'']]. The shorted-out shield generator would leave the droideka vulnerable.<ref name="ROTS novel">[[Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith (novelization)|''Star Wars'': Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'' novelization]]</ref> Also, in the rolling position, the droideka's shield could not be activated, leaving it vulnerable while rolling from place to place.<ref name="Battlefront II" />They were made after the failed grappling droideka design.

Droidekas had a hard time maneuvering on downward slopes and climbing up stairs. In their rolling configuration, they would have to go back quite a bit and then speed up, launching themselves up the stairs. They could also try to traverse stairs in walking configuration, although it was extremely hard for them to coordinate their three legs on stairs.<ref name="Episode I: The Visual Dictionary" />

Additionally, this droideka model, like the others, could not fire at targets in close proximity because its blasters were too far spread out.<ref name="Battlefront II" />

==History==
[[File:Q-series_droidekas.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Two Q-series droidekas on the [[Invisible Hand/Legends|''Invisible Hand'']]]]

The original design of this droideka was made by the insectoid [[Colicoid/Legends|Colicoids]] of [[Colla IV/Legends|Colla IV]], who were displeased by the limitations of [[Baktoid Combat Automata/Legends|Baktoid Combat Automata's]] basic [[B1-series battle droid/Legends|B1-series battle droid]]s, and chiefly manufactured there. The [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]] used trading in rare meats as a way to ease bargaining with the ravenously carnivorous Colicoids, and were able to get special rates on this normally very costly droid model.<ref name="Episode I: The Visual Dictionary" />

Before the Federation's defeat after the [[Invasion of Naboo/Legends|Invasion of Naboo]], the original droid model was usually slaved to a [[Central Control Computer/Legends|central computer]].<ref name="Episode I: The Visual Dictionary" /> This technique fell out of favor in the aftermath when they would function independently as the [[B2-series super battle droid/Legends|B2 super battle droids]] did.<ref name="aotc">{{Film|II}}</ref> However, the droidekas on [[Colla IV/Legends|Colla IV]] were not slaved to a central computer, making them independent. This made them much more expensive and deadlier.<ref name="Episode I: The Visual Dictionary" />

The Q-series droidekas operated independently as well, which was another one of their assets. They, like most other droideka models before them, were able to operate without being slaved to a central computer.<ref name="Episode I: The Visual Dictionary" />

During the early years of the Galactic Empire, many of these droidekas were used by [[Gizor Dellso]] in the [[Battle of Mustafar (Imperial Period)|Battle of Mustafar]]. All were destroyed when the Empire bombarded the planet.<ref name="Battlefront II" />

==Behind the scenes==
According to the [[Star Wars home video releases|DVD]] commentary of [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|''The Phantom Menace'']], a droideka's blaster is meant to sound similar to those of an [[All Terrain Armored Transport/Legends|All Terrain Armored Transport]]. This includes the Q-series droideka.<ref name="Star Wars Episode I: The Phantom Menace">{{Film|I}} ''DVD Commentary''</ref>
